sentiment.rationale: The document shows strong operational momentum with record revenues in equities and financing, a 71% YoY advisory revenue increase, and a 33% dividend increase, but forward guidance is not formally raised; management explicitly cautions that AWM results in H2 2025 will be 'more muted relative to our medium-term run rate expectations' and flags ongoing geopolitical and trade uncertainty. The score reflects genuine momentum (record financing revenues, rising backlog) tempered by explicit caution on H2 harvesting and no formal guidance raise.

summary.revenue: Net revenues of $14.6 billion for Q2 2025, reflecting performance across all major business segments.
summary.eps: Earnings per share of $10.91 for Q2 2025, after a $0.33 reduction from selected items disclosed by management.
summary.guidance: Management expects AWM results in H2 2025 to be 'more muted relative to our medium-term run rate expectations' due to a challenging harvesting environment. No formal full-year guidance raise was provided.
summary.margin: The firm achieved a 22% pre-tax margin in AWM for the first half of 2025; firm-wide pre-tax margin not explicitly stated.
key_risks: Modest net losses in private portfolio driven by markdowns in relation to certain real estate positions.
Provision for credit losses of $384 million primarily from charge-offs in the credit card portfolio, reflecting ongoing credit risk in consumer exposures.
Geopolitical concerns have intensified in many regions, notably in the Middle East.
Uncertainty around trade agreements and the ultimate impact on growth from higher tariffs.
Management expects AWM results in H2 2025 to be more muted relative to medium-term run rate expectations.
key_opportunities: Advisory backlog rose for a fifth consecutive quarter and is notably higher than 2024 year-end levels, supporting forward revenue visibility.
Equities net revenues reached a record $4.3 billion in Q2 2025, with intermediation up 45% YoY and financing up 23% YoY.
Total financing revenues set a new record for a sixth consecutive quarter, now comprising over one-third of fixed and equities revenues.
Assets under supervision reached a record $3.3 trillion, with $17 billion in long-term net inflows, marking the thirtieth consecutive quarter of fee-based net inflows.
Board approved a 33% increase in the quarterly dividend to $4 per share, reflecting confidence in durability of the franchise.
AI initiatives (GS AI assistant, Devan agentic AI) expected to drive efficiency and productivity.
